B is slightly better because tapping a step highlights the matching part, which ties the text to the diagram more directly, and its live SVG/HTML labels stay readable on phones. Neither answer explicitly says to label parts in place instead of decoding numbers. A is a little more scattered, with an extra energy-savings section and an optional pair of parallel lists. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers put the diagram first and number the steps to match it, and both name the specific parts of this appliance. B covers mobile layout more thoroughly: it has the diagram stack above the steps, keeps labels large and offers a simplified diagram. Its six steps follow the heat and water paths more cleanly, while A's last step combines two ideas. A's hover/tap highlighting is a nice way to tie the text to the diagram, but it doesn't make up for those gaps.
